Which Sony home console holds the record as the best-selling video game console of all time?
questions.explanation: The PlayStation 2, released in 2000, sold over 155 million units worldwide, making it the best-selling video game console in history. It dominated the market for years, outlasting many of its competitors and even continuing to sell well into the next console generation. Its massive library of games and DVD playback capability were key factors in its enormous success.

questions.question: Which classic Nintendo 64 adventure game, starring a young hero named Link, is one of the most popular titles in the speedrunning community?
questions.explanation: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is one of the most iconic speedrunning games ever, with runners exploiting glitches and optimized routes to complete it in record time. Speedrunning transforms single-player classics like this into a competitive, fast-paced experience. It adds an entirely new perspective on a game most players originally took dozens of hours to finish.

questions.question: Before Shigeru Miyamoto intervened to incorporate Fox McCloud into the project, what was the original working title of the game that eventually became Star Fox Adventures?
questions.explanation: Star Fox Adventures started life as an original Rare title called Dinosaur Planet, but Shigeru Miyamoto noticed similarities between its protagonist and Fox McCloud and suggested merging the two projects. The result was released on the GameCube in 2002 as Star Fox Adventures, one of the last games Rare developed before being acquired by Microsoft.

questions.question: Which Nintendo development division, known for producing landmark 3D platformers, completed its final full game with the globally released Super Mario Odyssey on October 27th, 2017?
questions.explanation: Nintendo EPD Tokyo (formerly EAD Tokyo) was the studio behind acclaimed titles like Super Mario Galaxy and Donkey Kong Jungle Beat before capping its run with Super Mario Odyssey in 2017. After Odyssey's release, the division was reorganized within Nintendo's EPD structure. The studio's legacy is defined by some of the most celebrated 3D platformers in gaming history.
